context.body: Ritual excess is contrasted with a known pattern of life before God.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The prophetic exchange rejects escalating offerings as the answer and recalls what the LORD requires: justice, mercy, and humble walking with God.
observations.label: God’s case narrows extravagant worship to faithful life: action

observations.body: The worshiper imagines costly gifts, even a firstborn, before the familiar requirement is stated.
observations.label: God’s case narrows extravagant worship to faithful life: response

observations.body: what shall I come with? · thousands of rams · do justice · walk humbly
observations.label: Words in Micah 6:6–8

payload.posture: Read Micah 6:6–8 as future and faithfulness evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The passage does not abolish every sacrifice; it denies that escalating gifts replace justice and covenant faithfulness.
payload.title: God’s case narrows extravagant worship to faithful life
